solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Flash and passionate, the man's lacking drive

parts.note: a flash is an instant, a mo in British slang

indicators.note: lacking says these letters go missing from the word for passionate

parts.note: passionate means vehement
the man is he; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone flashy and passionate who nevertheless lacks ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes HE out of VEHEMENT, leaving VEMENT. MO is British slang for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is an organised campaign, as is a movement for reform.

clue.text: Barbie's partner keeps his heart devoted

indicators.note: keeps means the doll's name holds a letter inside it

parts.note: Ken is the doll who partners Barbie
his refers to Ken, whose middle letter is E

explanation.surface: Barbie's boyfriend stays true to her at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his heart' means the centre of KEN itself, the letter E, so the name keeps a second copy of its own middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and devoted are both synonyms for being enthusiastic and committed.

clue.text: Spoil sermon sporadically getting pious

indicators.note: sporadically means only every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Ruining a sermon here and there while trying to look devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporadically' picks the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of SPOILSERMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious and solemn both describe grave, reverent religious seriousness.

clue.text: Fortune until cleaned out in old money

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the coins

parts.note: pence are coins, so money

indicators.note: cleaned out empties the word of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A fortune was held in old money until someone cleaned it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaned out' empties 'until' of its middle; 'in' sets what is left among the old coins. 'Fortune' reads as luck but means wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is great wealth, and opulence is lavish wealth or riches.

clue.text: Ringleader held in classroom as term in detention

indicators.note: held in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The class ringleader is kept in after school in detention all term.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'classroom' to the start of 'detention'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the planner behind a scheme, the person who masterminds it.

clue.text: Charges for jeans English imported

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Levi's are a well-known brand of jeans

explanation.surface: Duties charged on jeans imported from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imported' puts E inside LEVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Levies are taxes or duties, charges imposed by an authority.

clue.text: Keep holding back oddly stormier premier

indicators.note: holding means the stronghold contains the letters that follow

parts.note: a keep is a castle stronghold, a fort

indicators.note: back means the selected letters are read in reverse
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word stormier

explanation.surface: A stormier premier struggling to keep his grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters; 'back' reverses them; 'holding' sets them in the stronghold. 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the castle tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier and foremost both mean first in rank or leading.

clue.text: Start is long after tomorrow ends

indicators.note: after places the yearning word behind the two end letters
ends takes the first and last letters of the word tomorrow

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Waiting for tomorrow, the start feels a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes the outside letters of tomorrow and 'after' sets the yearning word behind them. 'Start' is a jump of surprise, not a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden involuntary jerk, which a twitch also is.

clue.text: Collect by trapping light beam

indicators.note: trapping means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: per means by, as in per hour
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Gathering things up by catching a ray of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a short prayer read in church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short liturgical prayer said on a set day in church.

clue.text: Resident fellow advanced in study

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the room

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: A college fellow living in, making progress with his research.
explanation.definitionFit: In a college a dean is a senior fellow who lives in and oversees discipline.

clue.text: It's needed to gorge large amount in inverted position?

definitions.text: It's needed to gorge large amount in inverted position?

indicators.note: in puts the eating words inside the turned place word
inverted means the place word is turned round

parts.note: a site is a position or location
to pig is to gorge on food
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: Something you need to be able to stuff yourself while upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' turns the place word round to ETIS, and 'in' puts the eating words inside it. Read whole, the clue describes the flap that keeps food out of the windpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is the throat flap that covers the windpipe so food goes down when swallowing.

clue.text: Liberal Government adopted by African country

indicators.note: adopted by means the letter is taken into the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A liberal regime installed in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' puts G inside BENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of generous and kindly is a synonym for benign.

clue.text: Whimpers on a ledge catching cold

indicators.note: catching means the run of words holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone stranded on a ledge whimpering as they catch a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like the illness being caught; it means unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is distant and unfeeling, lacking personal warmth.

clue.text: Gathering caught monster around end of Frankenstein

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: around means the monster wraps the letter that follows

parts.note: an ogress is a female monster

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers after a monster is caught circling Frankenstein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives N, which 'around' puts inside OGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A congress is a formal assembly or meeting, a gathering of delegates.

clue.text: Unfinished model case almost for disease

indicators.note: unfinished drops the final letter from the word for model

parts.note: a type is a model or pattern

indicators.note: almost loses the last letter of the word for case

parts.note: a husk is an outer case or shell

explanation.surface: An incomplete model of an almost-solved disease case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts TYPE to TYP; 'almost' cuts HUSK to HUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhus is an infectious fever spread by lice and fleas, so a disease.

clue.text: Moody daughter's left town

indicators.note: left means the letter has departed from the town's name

parts.note: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, England
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's reads as 'has'

explanation.surface: A sulky daughter has moved out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes D from DUNSTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moody has erratic, changeable emotions, which is to be emotionally erratic.

clue.text: Small redhead enfolding former girlfriend? That's more erotic!

indicators.note: enfolding means the two outer letters wrap around what follows

parts.note: the head of the word red is R
an ex is a former partner
i.e., id est, means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A petite redhead embracing her ex: steamier than expected!
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is not a link: it gives the abbreviation for id est. 'enfolding' sets the ex and that abbreviation between the two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of sexy describes something more sexually arousing, so more erotic.

clue.text: Comforted and felt again embracing sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing means the outer word wraps round the letter

parts.note: to relive something is to experience it again
the heart of sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Consoled as old feelings return while hugging a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the middle of sweet, E, which 'embracing' puts inside RELIVED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be comforted is to have one's anxiety eased, freed from worry.

clue.text: Deviation is severe with alien insertion

indicators.note: insertion means the alien letters are put into the stern word

parts.note: dour means stern or severe
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial, an alien

explanation.surface: A harsh deviation from routine after an alien is planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insertion' puts the film alien's two letters inside the stern word; 'is' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout route taken instead of the direct way.

clue.text: Aggressor calculated to hold back game

indicators.note: back means those letters are read in reverse
to hold says the two words contain the letters

explanation.surface: An attacker is calculating how to hold back in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the letters inside 'Aggressor calculated' give the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, so a game.

clue.text: Pensioners want one's consideration

parts.note: the elderly would like a person prejudiced against older people to think better of them

explanation.surface: Old folk asking for a bit of consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers to the answer: someone biased by age is the person pensioners need to think again.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person discriminates against people because of how old they are.

clue.text: Hooligan taking cover flipped altogether

indicators.note: flipped means the whole combination is read backwards
taking means the hooligan holds the cover inside

parts.note: a yob is a British slang term for a hooligan
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A lout grabs a lid and flips it over completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' sets the cover inside the lout to give YLIDOB, and 'flipped' reverses that whole string. 'altogether' means as one body, entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodily can mean as a whole, entirely, as in moving a building in one piece.

clue.text: Friendship involving the old raised in past

indicators.note: involving means the tie word contains the letters

parts.note: a bond is a tie of friendship

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: An old friendship rekindled after being brought up in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses the old form of 'the' to EY, as this is a down clue; 'involving' puts it inside the tie word. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond and past are prepositions both meaning further than a point.

clue.text: Offensive listing slaughter over in deadly case

indicators.note: in places the reversed words within those outside letters
case takes the outside letters of the word deadly
over means the joined words are turned round

parts.note: a rota is a listing of duties
gore is bloodshed, slaughter

explanation.surface: A grim listing of slaughter in a fatal case caused offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ROTAGORE into EROGATOR; 'case' gives DY from deadly to go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks are disparaging and insulting, hence offensive.

clue.text: Meat from grouse

definitions.meaning: flesh of the cow eaten as food

explanation.surface: Game bird served as the main course.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is cattle flesh, and as slang a beef is a complaint or a grumble.

clue.text: Throw piece of china

definitions.meaning: a round dish or basin made of porcelain

explanation.surface: Hurling a piece of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler throws the ball in cricket, and a china basin is a dish of that name.

clue.text: Slate mug — practically everybody's grabbing one

parts.note: a mug is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: grabbing means the shortened word holds the numeral inside
practically means nearly, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: everybody means all; the 's reads as 'is'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Criticise the fool: nearly everyone is getting hold of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' is British slang for criticising harshly. 'practically' cuts ALL to AL, which 'grabbing' wraps round I.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is to attack verbally, and to assail is to attack violently or with criticism.

clue.text: Prominent topless bird held as property

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the bird

parts.note: a wren is a small songbird
something held as property is owned

explanation.surface: A notable topless bird kept as someone's possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts WREN to REN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prominent is well known and celebrated, famous.
